item.title: Version 0.37.0
item.description:
Recall 0.37.0

---

Recall now understands parallel work

Until now, Recall assumed you did one thing at a time. If you jumped between a

code review, a Slack conversation, and a deploy, it mashed them into one

blurry thread. This release rebuilds tracking around how work actually

happens: each workstream gets its own thread, running side by side. The

menubar shows what you're focused on now, plus an "Also live" list of the

other things you have in flight. Time is counted honestly per stream — five

minutes in the code review is five minutes in the code review, even if Slack

was blinking next to it.

Projects that match reality

Project recognition was rebuilt from the ground up. Recall now derives your

projects from the actual shape of your work — which files, repos, pages, and

conversations genuinely belong together — instead of guessing from

co-occurrence alone.

What you'll notice:

  • Far fewer "Franken-projects." Work from two different projects that

happened to share an afternoon no longer gets fused into one card, and one

project can no longer silently swallow another's identity. If Recall thinks

two established projects might be the same thing, it suggests a merge in

Insights — you decide. It never merges them behind your back.

  • Fewer junk projects. A page you glanced at once, a Google search, a

meeting link — these no longer become "projects" that collect your real

work. Entertainment can't mint projects at all (see below).

  • Renames stick. If you rename a project, that name is yours — Recall

will never overwrite it.

Recognition for more than code

Project tracking used to be sharpest for developers — repos, files, branches.

This release brings that same first-class recognition to more kinds of work:

  • CRM work — a Salesforce or HubSpot account, deal, or contact you're

actually working on becomes its own project, grouped by the record instead

of lumped together as "that CRM tab."

  • Creative & office documents — Final Cut, Premiere, DaVinci, After

Effects, Logic, Photoshop, Illustrator, Sketch, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and

more. When Recall can see which document you have open, that document

anchors a real project — so an editor's timelines and a writer's docs get

the same treatment a developer's repos always had.

Nothing changes for the work Recall already recognized; this just widens the

net so more professions get real projects instead of a generic "app" bucket.

When Recall isn't sure, it says so

The biggest philosophical change in this release: Recall stopped guessing.

Work that can't be confidently placed goes to an "unassigned" state instead

of being forced into the nearest project. And a new on-device background

assistant quietly gathers evidence over time — as you keep working, it files

those unassigned items into the right project **only when several independent

signals agree**. Every automatic filing is logged and reversible. Nothing

leaves your Mac; it's the same local AI doing the thinking.

Finish tasks right from the panels

  • The Smart Return panel (the "welcome back" card) now has an

"I finished this" button — with a small celebration when you tap it,

because closure deserves one. The next thing worth returning to slides in

right after, so the momentum carries.

  • The "Too many threads. Pick one." panel got the same treatment — mark

things done or skip to the next suggestion right from the panel.

  • Finished work stays finished — it will never be suggested again, anywhere.
  • The Smart Return panel no longer disappears on a timer. It waits until

you decide: return, finish, or close.

  • Suggestions got smarter about duplicates: you won't be offered the same

title twice in a row, and duplicate topics with identical names now merge

automatically.

Browse any day, not just today

The Today view can now travel back in time: arrows and a calendar in the

header let you open any past day and see exactly what you worked on — same

cards, same stats, frozen as that day ended. "Today's work" becomes

"Tuesday's work" when you're looking at Tuesday.

Movies are not work

Recall finally knows the difference between doing things and watching

things. Searching for a film, downloading it, watching it — that's leisure

now, judged from what's actually on screen (not from a blocklist of apps, so

a video editor's timeline still counts as work):

  • Watching something while you have active work open counts as drift —

you'll get the same gentle nudge as any other distraction.

  • Watching something when nothing's active is simply a break. No task

card, no fake project, no nudge. Your reports stay clean.

Also fixed: real work that mentioned a pause was sometimes filed under

Breaks — no longer.

Untitled threads stay backstage

Threads no longer appear in the Today list as "Untitled Thread" — they show

up once they've earned a name. Less noise while work is still settling.

Opening Recall actually brings it to you

Clicking Today (or any menubar item) now pulls the window to the front, on

top of whatever you're using — no more window opening off on another desktop

where you can't find it. And while it's open, Recall shows up in the ⌘-Tab app

switcher like any normal app, so you can flip back to it the usual way.

Stability you'll feel

  • Restarts and crashes no longer eat your work. In-flight threads survive

an app restart or update with their time and context intact.

  • The overnight hang is gone. The on-device AI could previously wedge

under load and freeze tracking until you noticed (sometimes a whole night).

The root cause is fixed, and a watchdog now restarts the AI automatically

within a couple of minutes if anything like it ever happens again.

Your account page (joinrecall.com)

If you subscribed through our site (or use a partner code), you can now

add extra device slots from your account — half the price of your plan,

per device, cancel anytime from the same page. AppSumo licenses keep their

device counts managed through AppSumo, as before.

---

The theme of this release

Recall trusts evidence, not guesses. It watches how your work actually

clusters, admits when it doesn't know, corrects itself when it learns better,

and leaves every decision inspectable and reversible. Less cleanup, fewer

surprises, and a dashboard that looks like your real week.

item.title: Version 0.33.1
item.description:
Recall 0.33.1

Critical fix: this resolves a crash that stopped 0.32.0 and 0.33.0 from running — the app would launch, then vanish from the menu bar a moment later with no error or alert. If you were on 0.32.0 or 0.33.0, this update restores a working build with all of their features included (they're listed below, since those releases never actually ran for most people).

Fixes

  • fix(launch): app crashed silently shortly after launch — the Public Suffix List loaded through the wrong resource accessor on shipped builds, which aborted the first project-consolidation tick

Context coherence (carried over from 0.33.0)

  • feat(context): per-window project identity on snapshots — Smart Return and the context stack no longer bleed in off-project windows
  • fix(labeling): drop uncorroborated title tokens from thread labels — a stale conversation title no longer leaks into the label
  • fix(restore): restore + preview now filter off-project windows, matching the context stack

Project consolidation & splitting (carried over from 0.32.0)

  • feat(consolidation): split mixed projects apart — split judge prompt + planner with a reversible audit trail
  • feat(consolidation): web projects anchored by registrable domain; jira grouped by ticket prefix; localhost/IP by host
  • feat(consolidation): dominant-token anchoring + star-merge, key-aware rename, same-name deterministic merge
  • feat(consolidation): cross-anchor merge judge + guarded LLM backfill
  • feat(loops): Open Loops inbox — stalest-first unresolved topics, in a new Loops tab

Other improvements (carried over from 0.32.0)

  • feat(feedback): paste clipboard image attachments with Cmd-V
  • feat(today): drillable "Other" card with one-level back navigation
  • fix(insights): focus-modes heatmap now driven by real behavior data
  • fix(smart-return): return to the live thread from the tray, not the dashboard
  • fix(capture): the active task now switches correctly between concurrent Claude conversations in one folder
  • fix(focus): "foggy" no longer bleeds into productive work after a foggy spell
  • fix(today): the "Other" bucket no longer opens the wrong thread

item.title: Version 0.31.0
item.description:
Recall 0.31.0

Improved

  • Task switching that actually works. When you move between different Claude Code conversations in the same project, Recall now opens a fresh, correctly-named thread for the new task — instead of the previous task's label following you around. The earlier detection couldn't tell a genuine task switch from the same task reworded; this version uses the conversation itself as the signal, so the switch is recognised reliably.

item.title: Version 0.30.0
item.description:
Recall 0.30.0

New

  • Tasks you can check off. Every task now has a checkbox on the Today and project pages (and in the Smart Return panel) — tick to mark it done, untick to reopen. An Active / Done filter keeps finished tasks tucked away by default.
  • Finished tasks complete themselves. When Recall sees an on-screen confirmation (a form submitted, an email sent, a PR merged), it quietly marks a small, single-task topic done instead of nagging you about it for days. Bigger topics aren't touched — the finished piece just stops resurfacing.
  • Smarter task switching. Moving to a genuinely different task inside the same project now opens a fresh, correctly-named thread, instead of carrying the previous task's label around with you.

Fixes

  • No more drift nudges while you're away. A distraction reminder can no longer fire minutes into an idle gap about something that already ended.
  • Chat attachments stop hijacking labels. A pinned Telegram/Slack file no longer gets mistaken for the file you're working on — your coding session keeps its real name.
  • Your work isn't mislabeled as leisure. Startup/outreach work on sites like LinkedIn reads as work (not a break) once Recall has tied it to one of your projects — while mindless scrolling on the same site still counts as drift.

item.title: Version 0.29.0
item.description:
Recall 0.29.0

A test build for our testers. What's new since 0.28.0:

Improvements

  • Sharper, leaner screen understanding. Capture now focuses on the active window and skips frames with nothing to read, so the on-device model sees more detail where it matters — better at reading file names, ticket numbers, and titles — while doing less work.
  • Smarter distraction detection — and fairer across the board.

- A quick Slack/email interruption while you're working is no longer misread as a distraction (it's an interruption, handled differently).

- Distraction detection now works for web-based work too — if your day lives in web apps (support consoles, accounting, CRM, recruiting), drifting off to unrelated video/social is now caught, the same way it already was for file-based work.

Under the hood

  • The full pipeline (focus modes, session grouping, distraction, labeling, project consolidation) is now validated against a large synthetic dataset spanning many professions — so behavior is checked for non-developer work, not just coding.

_Please flag anything that feels off — a distraction that wasn't caught (or a focused session wrongly flagged), wrong project grouping, or an odd activity label._

item.title: Version 0.28.0
item.description:
Recall 0.28.0

A test build for our testers. Highlights you can feel:

Improvements

  • Better distraction detection. Watching unrelated TV/YouTube is now correctly recognized as a break even when your actual work involves video or research — generic overlaps ("video", "content") no longer shelter off-topic viewing.
  • Smarter communication grouping. Chat and email activity is now annotated with the project it's actually about, so your day reads more coherently in the report.
  • Clearer activity descriptions. The on-screen analysis names the real task from the window/conversation headline instead of fixating on a prominent-but-secondary detail, reads chats by their messages, and avoids inventing outcomes.

Under the hood

  • A large synthetic test corpus across many professions now exercises the full pipeline, so behavior is validated for non-developer work (design, marketing, support, legal, etc.), not just coding.

_Please report anything that feels off — wrong project grouping, a distraction that wasn't flagged (or a focused session wrongly flagged), or an odd activity label._

item.title: Version 0.15.1
item.description:
Recall 0.15.1

Fixes

  • Fixed a crash when opening Settings → Acknowledgements. The licenses screen could crash the app on open; it now loads correctly.
  • Fewer freezes / beachballs. Recall no longer does a filesystem search on the main thread while you work, which was causing intermittent multi-second hangs.
  • Diagnostics uploads now work as intended. Opting into Diagnostics now reliably captures and uploads the full session (including the AI's screenshots and decisions); a bug left the richest data permanently empty.
  • Inference stability. Hardened the on-device model against a couple of crashes — a closed-connection signal and a rare empty-frame case (e.g. on lock screen / display changes).

Privacy

  • Crash reports no longer include your name or hostname. Recall's automatic crash/error reporting now identifies your install only by a random ID, sending just your macOS version and Mac model for triage — and this is now disclosed in Settings → Privacy and the bundled notices.

item.title: Version 0.15.0
item.description:
Recall 0.15.0

Features

  • Work Summary — a new Summary tab gives you a daily work recap written by the on-device AI: a short overview of how the day went, what moved forward, and what's still open. Generate or refresh it whenever you like (today refreshes at most every couple of hours); step back through past days to read their recaps. Once a day is over, its summary is captured and frozen.

Improvements

  • Modes are easier to reach on Apple-silicon Macs — the live mode signals now track Recall's actual capture rhythm, so interruptions and other states register correctly on machines that analyze less frequently. M3/M4 (base) Macs now also run analysis at the faster cadence.
  • Cleaner main window — removed the redundant Mode Breakdown strip from Focus, the deterministic and Efforts panels from Today, and the separate Reports tab. The work-shape card and your daily recap are the home for that information now.

Notes

  • The Summary recap is generated only when you ask for it, and like everything in Recall it's produced on-device.

item.title: Version 0.14.0
item.description:
Recall 0.14.0

Features

  • Opt-in diagnostics sharing — a new switch in Settings → Privacy lets you help fix Recall by sharing what it saw and decided when something goes wrong. It's off by default and stays off unless you turn it on. When enabled, Recall uploads (encrypted, to EU storage, auto-deleted after 30 days) the screenshots its AI analyzed, the AI's inputs and outputs, app/window activity, and its own mode decisions — identified only by a random ID, never your name or email. A confirmation screen spells out exactly what's collected before anything leaves your Mac, and you can turn it off at any time (which stops uploads and deletes the local queue immediately). While it's on, the app says so plainly.

Internal

  • Continuous tailing of the full replay stream (LLM traces + images + DB deltas + runtime mode/panel decisions) so issues can be reproduced exactly; write-only upload credential, server-side 30-day retention.

item.title: Version 0.13.0
item.description:
Recall 0.13.0

Features

  • Recall now learns your work shape — the Focus page shows an inferred work type ("Product builder", "Engineer-coder"…) with a confidence level, your primary apps, most active hours, secondary signals, and how you best return to work after breaks. It's judged weekly by the on-device AI from a 30-day evidence summary — aggregates only, never raw screen content — and like everything in Recall it never leaves your Mac.
  • Confidence is earned, not asserted: the first assessment caps at Medium, and the label only reaches High after consecutive weekly runs agree. Until there's about a week of activity, the card simply says it's still learning.

Internal

  • The work profile is the first surface of Recall's profession-neutrality work: the same evidence will later teach the classifier what counts as work for you specifically — whether your work lives in code, design files, chats, or calls.

item.title: Version 0.12.1
item.description:
Recall 0.12.1

Fixes

  • Slack huddles are now treated as meetings — joining a huddle from focused work silently saves your dropped thread, exactly like a Zoom call. Previously huddles ran through the chat path and could end with a "you drifted" nudge mid-call.
  • Long calls never nudge — meetings of any length stay silent until they end. Previously a call longer than ~10 minutes could fall back into drift detection.
  • Leisure browsing can no longer pass as work via a single coincidental word — a TikTok video about "video editing" no longer counts as on-task just because your real work shares one word with it. Genuinely work-related content on the same sites still classifies correctly.

item.title: Version 0.12.0
item.description:
Recall 0.12.0

Performance

  • Screen analysis is now 2.4x faster on M1/M2 — 17s → ~7s end-to-end steady state (M3 Pro: ~4.1s → ~2.6s). On top of 0.11.0's fp16 + KV-cache groundwork, this release restructures the prompt so the static instructions ride in a cached system message instead of being re-processed on every frame, and stops the chat template from injecting ~530 tokens of model boilerplate per request.
  • Thread labeling and project classification are ~20% faster — every text prompt was paying the same boilerplate tax; now none do.
  • Less GPU time per frame also means lower power draw during all-day tracking.

Notes

  • The first 1–2 analyses after the app starts run a few seconds slower than steady state while the cache warms up — everything after that is fast.
  • Analysis quality is verified equivalent: same outputs on test screenshots, JSON structure intact.

item.title: Version 0.11.0
item.description:
Recall 0.11.0

Features

  • Reactive mode now works — when a chat ping or a meeting pulls you out of focused work, Recall detects the interruption the minute it happens and silently saves your dropped thread so it's waiting for you when you come back. Meetings no longer trigger a "you drifted" nudge mid-call — a call that interrupts your work is treated as an interruption, not a distraction. If a quick reply turns into a 10+ minute chat spiral, the gentle drift nudge still has your back.

Performance

  • Screen analysis is dramatically faster — roughly 2x on M1/M2 (17s → ~9.5s steady state) and ~20% on M3 Pro (~4.1s → ~3.4s). Three changes: fp16 weights (M1/M2 GPUs emulate bf16, so fp16 halves the prefill cost at verified-equivalent quality), a prompt-prefix KV cache (the static instruction block is prefilled once and reused on every request), and captures downscaled to the model's own 1024px input cap before sending. Lower latency also means less GPU time per frame — better battery.

Internal

  • Reactive detection rewrote the classifier's interruption rule from an unreachable 5-minute state ratio to a 90-second edge detector with a bounded 10-minute hold; a tick-by-tick reachability regression test now guards it.

item.title: Version 0.10.0
item.description:
Recall 0.10.0

Features

  • Foggy mode detection — Recall now notices when you've been on one project for a while without actually moving forward (re-reading, file-hopping, staring) and gently surfaces a single anchor card to help you re-engage. Detection is deliberately strict: a lightweight on-device signal must hold for 15 minutes straight and the on-device AI must independently confirm the work is stalled before anything appears — genuine deep work is never interrupted. Dismissing the card keeps it away for 30 minutes.

Internal

  • Mode classification consolidated onto the live deterministic classifier; the legacy bucket-based routing path was removed (~500 lines deleted, all tests migrated).

item.title: Version 0.9.3
item.description:
What's new in 0.9.3

Cleaner thread titles. Browsing and AI-chat threads no longer show a raw internal identifier (like web:chatgpt.com/c/…) on the Today, tray, or Smart Return cards — you now see the actual task you were working on.

Labels stay on-topic. A brief detour into an unrelated tab can no longer hijack a thread's title, and labels written early now refresh as the thread grows — so a session of real work doesn't end up named after a stray tab you glanced at.

Smart Return reopens the right workspace. Returning to a thread now restores the workspace that matches that thread, instead of whichever one happened to be open last.

item.title: Version 0.9.2
item.description:
What's new in 0.9.2

Fix: returning to a thread now reliably brings the app to the front, instead of opening it in the background.

item.title: Version 0.9.1
item.description:
What's new in 0.9.1

Polish: focus prompts are now labeled correctly for each situation, so the prompt you see always matches what Recall is actually nudging you about.

item.title: Version 0.9.0
item.description:
What's new in 0.9.0

Smarter distraction detection. Recall now understands when you've genuinely drifted to something unrelated to your work — and stays quiet when what you're looking at is relevant to it — instead of relying on a fixed list of "distracting" sites. Whatever your work is, Recall judges drift against that.

Better "come back" nudges. When you drift, the gentle nudge now names what you were working on, doesn't interrupt once you've already returned, and reappears if a long distraction keeps going.

Smoother one-click return. Returning to a thread now brings an already-open app or browser tab to the front instead of opening a duplicate.

Plus reliability fixes to the focus engine and nudge display.

item.title: Version 0.8.0
item.description:
Recall 0.8.0

New: Efforts — your work, grouped by product

Recall now groups your related projects into the real products and initiatives they belong to. Code repos, web apps, dashboards, and team channels that belong to the same product roll up into a single effort — automatically, on‑device, with no manual tagging. See it in the new Efforts today panel on the Today tab.

It groups only what your activity supports — deterministic identity from your repos and URLs plus distinctive concepts from your topics — entirely on your device.

Improved

  • More accurate project attribution — when you bounce between projects, a session is attributed to the work you were focused on, not whichever had the most frames.
  • Cleaner Today view — your distinct projects show as separate cards with real titles.
  • Leaner, faster on‑device analysis — fewer fields per frame; the active file name is read from the OS rather than guessed.
  • Concise re‑entry and drift cards.

Fixed

  • Thread labels and topics could stop updating when a backlog of empty sessions built up. Fixed.
  • Overloaded mode now nudges when you're juggling several projects.
  • Projects served on different localhost ports are no longer merged together.

item.title: Version 0.7.3
item.description:
Recall 0.7.3

Improvements

  • Smart Return suggests browser projects the same day. If you put real time (25+ min) into a browser-based project — research, analytics, a web app — Smart Return can now bring it back the same day, instead of waiting until you've worked on it across two separate days.

item.title: Version 0.7.2
item.description:
Recall 0.7.2

Fixes

  • Drift nudges now name what you were working on. When you stepped away — say, into a meeting — the "you drifted" nudge showed a generic "your last thread." It now names the actual project or task you left, so it's clear what to come back to.

item.title: Version 0.7.1
item.description:
Recall 0.7.1

Fixes

  • Smart Return now appears after an overnight or weekend break. Opening your laptop in the morning is the most common moment to want "here's where you left off" — but Recall was only looking back 8 hours, so after a longer gap it surfaced nothing. It now reliably brings back your most recent thread after overnight and weekend breaks.

item.title: Version 0.7.0
item.description:
Recall 0.7.0

New

  • New on-device AI model — Ministral-3. Screen understanding now runs on Mistral AI's Ministral-3 vision model (replacing Qwen 3.5-VL) for faster, more reliable frame analysis. It auto-downloads on first launch.
  • Project tracking for browser-only work. If you mostly work in a browser (marketing, research, analytics, AI assistants), Recall now builds Projects and Smart Return for you too — provisional projects form from what you're actually working on and mature into full projects over time. Still no manual tagging.

Improvements

  • Video meetings now count as interruptions. Zoom / Google Meet / Teams calls drop focus and surface a drift nudge; async chat (Slack, etc.) stays "reactive" and is saved silently.
  • Smart Return appears promptly on return. Fixed a bug where coming back from a long break could leave the re-entry panel ~1 min late or missing entirely.
  • "Too many threads" only when truly overloaded — now requires 3+ distinct projects instead of firing on a single thread.
  • Saved-for-later threads always resurface on return, even without an assigned topic.

Under the hood

  • Faster inference (1024px frames + VisionZip), chat-template fix, image token-cache (VLCache), helper-process hardening.
  • Removed the legacy screenshot-captures debug store (reclaims significant disk).
